32	/**
33	 * Northgate Family Medicine — chart event log, version 1.
34	 *
35	 * Northgate is a primary-care practice. Its EHR keeps the chart as an append-only log of small
36	 * events, and publishes each event as one FOLIO record item: one signed visit note, one vital-sign
37	 * set, one medication change, one problem-list change, one allergy-list change, one list review,
38	 * one interfaced lab result report, one referral step, or one void.
39	 *
40	 * Most items carry exactly one payload entry. Three kinds carry several: an imported result report has
41	 * one entry per result component (a renal panel has a creatinine entry and one or more eGFR entries); a
42	 * signed visit note has its `visit` entry plus one `billing_dx` entry per billed diagnosis; a referral
43	 * step has its `referral_event` entry plus one `referral_dx` entry per diagnosis on the referral.
44	 * Diagnoses are separate entries, never lists inside another entry, so a patient can share a visit note
45	 * or referral while withholding one diagnosis (for example a behavioral-health code).
46	 *
47	 * There is no "current state" record. The current medication list, problem list and allergy list
48	 * are what you get by replaying the events in `effective` order for each list-line id (`med_id`,
49	 * `problem_id`, `allergy_id`), after dropping items that were retracted or superseded.
50	 *
51	 * Conventions that apply to every entry type:
52	 * - Times carry an offset. Northgate is in America/Chicago (-06:00 standard, -05:00 daylight).
53	 * - Item narrative is what the clinician typed into the event's comment box or signed as a note.
54	 *   It is never generated from the payload. Many items have no narrative.
55	 * - `visit_id`, where present, is Northgate's visit number (e.g. "V-2024-111203"). It groups the
56	 *   events entered during one visit. Absent for events entered outside a visit (interfaced
57	 *   results, phone refills, chart corrections).
58	 * - Items received through the lab interface have no `author`; every other item's author is the
59	 *   Northgate user who entered it.
60	 */
61	
62	/** One entry in a Northgate item. Discriminated by `type`. */
63	export type ChartEvent =
64	  | Visit
65	  | VitalSet
66	  | MedEvent
67	  | ProblemEvent
68	  | AllergyEvent
69	  | BillingDx
70	  | ListReviewed
71	  | ImportedResult
72	  | ReferralEvent
73	  | ReferralDx
74	  | ChartCorrection;
75	
76	/**
77	 * Restricted-chart category. Northgate hides restricted entries from users without the matching
78	 * privilege and excludes them from routine outbound records unless the patient consents.
79	 * - 'BH': behavioral health (depression, anxiety, and the medications used for them).
80	 * Absent means not restricted. The flag is set by the clinician when the entry is created and
81	 * restated on every later event for the same list line.
82	 */
83	export type Restriction = 'BH';
84	
85	/**
86	 * A full date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) with how much of it is real. Northgate's date picker always stores a
87	 * full date; when the clinician knows only the year or month, it fills the rest with 01 and records
88	 * the precision. So `{ date: "2016-01-01", precision: "year" }` means "sometime in 2016", not
89	 * January 1st.
90	 */
91	export interface FuzzyDate {
92	  /** Always a full date. Days and months beyond `precision` are filler (`01`). */
93	  date: string;
94	  /**
95	   * How much of `date` is meaningful.
96	   * - 'year': only the year is known.
97	   * - 'month': year and month are known.
98	   * - 'day': the full date is known.
99	   */
100	  precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day';
101	}
102	
103	/**
104	 * A visit note: the clinician's signed note for one office, telehealth or nurse visit. The item
105	 * narrative is the note itself, which is usually a few terse lines. The visit's billing diagnoses are
106	 * `billing_dx` entries in the same item. The structured events from the same visit (vitals, medication
107	 * and problem changes) are separate items sharing the `visit_id`.
108	 */
109	export interface Visit {
110	  type: 'visit';
111	
112	  /** Northgate visit number. Stable; every event entered during this visit carries it. */
113	  visit_id: string;
114	
115	  /**
116	   * Kind of visit.
117	   * - 'office': in-person visit with a clinician.
118	   * - 'telehealth': video visit.
119	   * - 'nurse': nurse-only visit (BP check, injection teaching). No clinician exam.
120	   * - 'phone': documented phone encounter.
121	   */
122	  visit_type: 'office' | 'telehealth' | 'nurse' | 'phone';
123	
124	  /** Reason for visit as typed at scheduling or check-in, e.g. "Hosp f/u". Free text. */
125	  reason: string;
126	}
127	
128	/**
129	 * One billing diagnosis of a visit, in the visit note's item (one entry per code). These are what was
130	 * billed, not the problem list: a code here does not add, change or confirm a problem. Follow-up and
131	 * screening codes (Z codes) appear here and never on the problem list.
132	 */
133	export interface BillingDx {
134	  type: 'billing_dx';
135	
136	  /** The visit billed (the `visit` entry in the same item). */
137	  visit_id: string;
138	
139	  /** Position on the claim, 1 = primary. */
140	  rank: number;
141	
142	  /** ICD-10-CM code, with the dot. */
143	  icd10cm: string;
144	
145	  /** Northgate's display text for the code. */
146	  display: string;
147	
148	  /** Restricted-chart category; see `Restriction`. Set on behavioral-health codes. */
149	  restricted?: Restriction;
150	}
151	
152	/**
153	 * One set of vital signs taken together, usually by a medical assistant at check-in. Any member
154	 * may be absent when it was not measured. Values are as entered on the flowsheet; nothing is
155	 * derived (BMI is not stored).
156	 */
157	export interface VitalSet {
158	  type: 'vital_set';
159	
160	  /** Visit the set was taken at. Absent for a stand-alone BP check logged outside a visit. */
161	  visit_id?: string;
162	
163	  /**
164	   * Blood pressure as typed on the flowsheet: text "systolic/diastolic" in mmHg, e.g. "152/94".
165	   * Always two integers separated by "/". Absent if not taken.
166	   */
167	  bp?: string;
168	
169	  /**
170	   * A second blood pressure taken later in the same visit, same text form as `bp`. Present only
171	   * when the first was high and the MA repeated it. Both readings are valid measurements.
172	   */
173	  bp_repeat?: string;
174	
175	  /**
176	   * Patient position for `bp` and `bp_repeat`.
177	   * - 'sitting', 'standing', 'supine': as recorded. Absent means not recorded (almost always sitting).
178	   */
179	  bp_position?: 'sitting' | 'standing' | 'supine';
180	
181	  /** Pulse, beats per minute. */
182	  pulse_bpm?: number;
183	
184	  /** Weight in pounds, clothed, clinic scale. One decimal place. */
185	  weight_lb?: number;
186	
187	  /** Height in inches. Usually measured once a year; absent otherwise. */
188	  height_in?: number;
189	
190	  /** Oral temperature, degrees Fahrenheit. */
191	  temp_f?: number;
192	
193	  /** Pulse oximetry, percent, room air. */
194	  spo2_pct?: number;
195	}
196	
197	/**
198	 * One change to one line of the medication list: started, dose changed, held, resumed, stopped,
199	 * or added from an outside record. Every event restates the whole order line as it stands after
200	 * the event (on a 'stop' or 'hold', the line as it was when stopped or held), so a single event is
201	 * readable on its own.
202	 */
203	export interface MedEvent {
204	  type: 'med_event';
205	
206	  /**
207	   * Northgate medication-list line id, e.g. "ML-30418". Stable across all events for one line.
208	   * A drug that is stopped and later restarted gets a new line id.
209	   */
210	  med_id: string;
211	
212	  /**
213	   * What happened to the line.
214	   * - 'start': line created; the patient should start (or, for medications already taken at the
215	   *   first Northgate visit, is already taking) the drug.
216	   * - 'change': dose, frequency or sig changed; the line stays active.
217	   * - 'hold': paused with intent to resume. The line stays on Northgate's list, shown "On hold";
218	   *   the patient should not be taking it. A hold does not expire on its own: it lasts until a
219	   *   'resume' or 'stop' event, however long that takes.
220	   * - 'resume': a held line is active again.
221	   * - 'stop': discontinued. Final for this line; a restart is a new 'start' with a new `med_id`.
222	   * Held is not stopped and not active. Only the latest event per `med_id` says where a line stands.
223	   */
224	  action: 'start' | 'change' | 'hold' | 'resume' | 'stop';
225	
226	  /**
227	   * Where the line came from.
228	   * - 'northgate': prescribed or managed by a Northgate clinician.
229	   * - 'outside': entered during medication reconciliation from another organization's record
230	   *   (e.g. a Lakeview nephrology visit summary). Northgate does not manage it and learns of
231	   *   changes only when someone reconciles again, so outside lines can lag the prescriber's record.
232	   */
233	  origin: 'northgate' | 'outside';
234	
235	  /**
236	   * The drug.
237	   * - `name`: display name as on the order, e.g. "losartan 50 MG Oral Tablet".
238	   * - `rxnorm`: RxNorm CUI (SCD or SBD) from Northgate's drug file. Present for Northgate-prescribed
239	   *   lines; often absent for 'outside' lines, which carry only `outside_code`.
240	   * - `outside_code`: the other organization's drug identifier as it appeared in their record,
241	   *   with `system` naming that organization's code space (e.g. "lakeview-drug"). Present only on
242	   *   'outside' lines. Not mapped to RxNorm.
243	   */
244	  drug: {
245	    name: string;
246	    rxnorm?: string;
247	    outside_code?: { system: string; code: string };
248	  };
249	
250	  /**
251	   * Amount per dose. `unit` is Northgate's dose unit text: "mg", "units" (insulin), or "tab".
252	   * Absent when the sig cannot be expressed as one amount (e.g. sliding scale).
253	   */
254	  dose?: { value: number; unit: string };
255	
256	  /**
257	   * Northgate frequency code.
258	   * - 'QD': once daily. 'BID': twice daily. 'TID': three times daily.
259	   * - 'QHS': once daily at bedtime. 'PRN': as needed. 'OTHER': see `sig`.
260	   */
261	  frequency?: 'QD' | 'BID' | 'TID' | 'QHS' | 'PRN' | 'OTHER';
262	
263	  /** Patient instructions exactly as printed on the prescription, e.g. "Take 1 tablet by mouth daily". */
264	  sig?: string;
265	
266	  /**
267	   * Why the line was stopped. Present on every 'stop'; absent on other actions.
268	   * - 'adverse_reaction': stopped because of a side effect or adverse reaction. A matching
269	   *   allergy-list event (`allergy_event`) is usually entered the same day, but not always.
270	   * - 'ineffective': not working well enough.
271	   * - 'therapy_changed': replaced by a different drug for the same purpose.
272	   * - 'course_complete': finite course finished.
273	   * - 'patient_choice': patient declined to continue.
274	   * - 'other': see `reason_text`.
275	   */
276	  stop_reason?: 'adverse_reaction' | 'ineffective' | 'therapy_changed' | 'course_complete' | 'patient_choice' | 'other';
277	
278	  /** Clinician's free-text reason for this event. Common on 'stop', 'hold' and 'change'; rare on 'start'. */
279	  reason_text?: string;
280	
281	  /**
282	   * On 'hold' only: the date the prescriber plans to review the hold. A planning date, not an
283	   * automatic resume; absent when no date was given.
284	   */
285	  review_on?: string;
286	
287	  /** Restricted-chart category; see `Restriction`. */
288	  restricted?: Restriction;
289	
290	  /** Visit the event was entered at; absent for phone refills and reconciliation outside a visit. */
291	  visit_id?: string;
292	}
293	
294	/**
295	 * One change to one line of the problem list. The problem list is maintained by hand: a line
296	 * changes only when a clinician edits it, so a line can be out of date with respect to newer
297	 * results or other organizations' diagnoses (see `ListReviewed` for why a review does not mean the
298	 * line is current).
299	 */
300	export interface ProblemEvent {
301	  type: 'problem_event';
302	
303	  /** Northgate problem-list line id, e.g. "PL-11902". Stable across all events for one line. */
304	  problem_id: string;
305	
306	  /**
307	   * What happened to the line.
308	   * - 'add': line created.
309	   * - 'update': description, codes or onset edited. Staging changes are made this way (the line
310	   *   keeps its id), so the latest 'update' carries the current wording.
311	   * - 'resolve': problem no longer active; the line moves to Past Medical History.
312	   * - 'remove': line deleted from the list because it was wrong (not because the problem resolved).
313	   */
314	  action: 'add' | 'update' | 'resolve' | 'remove';
315	
316	  /** Problem as displayed on the list, e.g. "Chronic kidney disease stage 3a". Restated on every event. */
317	  description: string;
318	
319	  /** ICD-10-CM code chosen when the line was created or last updated. */
320	  icd10cm: string;
321	
322	  /** SNOMED CT concept from Northgate's terminology service. Absent for lines created before 2020. */
323	  snomed?: string;
324	
325	  /** When the problem began, with precision. Often year-only for problems that predate Northgate. */
326	  onset?: FuzzyDate;
327	
328	  /** Restricted-chart category; see `Restriction`. */
329	  restricted?: Restriction;
330	
331	  /** Visit the event was entered at, if any. */
332	  visit_id?: string;
333	}
334	
335	/**
336	 * One change to one line of the allergy list. Northgate's allergy list holds allergies,
337	 * intolerances and adverse reactions in one list; `reaction_type` says which.
338	 */
339	export interface AllergyEvent {
340	  type: 'allergy_event';
341	
342	  /** Northgate allergy-list line id, e.g. "AL-2207". Stable across events for one line. */
343	  allergy_id: string;
344	
345	  /**
346	   * What happened to the line.
347	   * - 'add': line created.
348	   * - 'update': reaction, severity or comment edited.
349	   * - 'inactivate': no longer considered valid (e.g. patient tolerated a re-challenge). The line
350	   *   stays in history.
351	   */
352	  action: 'add' | 'update' | 'inactivate';
353	
354	  /**
355	   * The substance. `rxnorm` is an RxNorm ingredient CUI for drugs; absent for foods and
356	   * environmental allergens, which have `name` only.
357	   */
358	  substance: { name: string; rxnorm?: string };
359	
360	  /**
361	   * Kind of reaction, as chosen by the clinician.
362	   * - 'allergy': immune-mediated (hives, angioedema, anaphylaxis).
363	   * - 'intolerance': non-immune, predictable side effect that made the drug unacceptable (e.g.
364	   *   ACE-inhibitor cough). Not an allergy.
365	   * - 'adverse_reaction': a serious harmful event attributed to the drug that is not an allergy
366	   *   (e.g. drug-associated ketoacidosis).
367	   */
368	  reaction_type: 'allergy' | 'intolerance' | 'adverse_reaction';
369	
370	  /** Reactions from Northgate's picklist, display text, e.g. ["Cough"]. At least one. */
371	  reactions: string[];
372	
373	  /**
374	   * Northgate's "severity" field, which is really criticality: how dangerous re-exposure is
375	   * judged to be, not how bad the past reaction was.
376	   * - 'low': re-exposure unlikely to cause serious harm.
377	   * - 'high': re-exposure could be serious or life-threatening.
378	   * - 'unknown': not assessed.
379	   */
380	  severity: 'low' | 'high' | 'unknown';
381	
382	  /** When the reaction began, with precision. Absent if not recorded. */
383	  onset?: FuzzyDate;
384	
385	  /** Visit the event was entered at, if any. */
386	  visit_id?: string;
387	}

391	 * changed. This records that the list was looked at, not that each line was re-confirmed: a
392	 * stale line stays stale after a review.
393	 */

395	  type: 'list_reviewed';
396	
397	  /**
398	   * Which list was reviewed.
399	   * - 'problems', 'medications', 'allergies': the corresponding Northgate list.

405	
406	  /** Visit the review happened at. */

411	 * One result component received through Northgate's lab interface from Lakeview Labs and filed in
412	 * Northgate's chart. Northgate issues its own copy: the same result also exists in Lakeview's own
413	 * records under Lakeview's identifiers, and `external_ref` points to it. One item holds every

417	 * interface translation table (see `unit`).

420	 * never appear here.
421	 *
422	 * When Lakeview sends a correction for a report Northgate already filed, Northgate publishes a new
423	 * item that `supersedes` the old one and restates every component of the report as corrected, with

425	 * a replacement, as for a hemolyzed specimen: the corrected component then has a non-numeric `value`

431	
432	  /**

434	   * - `nfm_code`: Northgate result-component code, e.g. "CREAT", "EGFR-NAA". Assigned by Northgate's

441	  test: { nfm_code: string; name: string; loinc?: string };

content.text:
I wrote `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks, and it runs on the sample patients with sensible output. The samples are small, so the harder cases are untested: holds, restricted behavioral-health lines, CKD staging, and unit conversion.

Judgment calls:

- **Which items count.** An item counts if its `recorded` local date in America/Chicago is on or before `asOf`. Retractions come from the envelope `retracts` and from `voided_items`. Supersession is followed through chains. A retracted item's own `supersedes` is ignored, so it replaces nothing.
- **Latest event per line.** Medication, problem and allergy lines take their state from the latest event by `effective`, then `recorded`.
  - A hold stays held until a later event says otherwise.
  - For an active medication, `status_since` is the date of its last start or resume.
  - A problem with a `remove` event is dropped, and an allergy with `inactivate` is dropped.
  - Billing and referral diagnoses never become problems.
- **Medications.**
  - One row per ingredient, taken from the line whose latest event is most recent.
  - The ingredient is parsed from the order name, with salts, strengths and forms stripped.
  - `rxnorm_ingredient` is always omitted, because the source codes are product-level.
  - A dose in "tab" becomes strength × count in mg when the order name gives a strength; otherwise it stays in tablets.
  - Restricted-chart "BH" lines get the `mental-health` tag.
- **Problems.**
  - `ckd_stage` and `albuminuria` come from the latest wording first, then the ICD code. Stage 3 with no a/b letter gives no stage.
  - A T36–T50 adverse-effect code produces an allergy row only.
  - A "due to <drug>" description produces both rows, but only if the drug appears elsewhere in the patient's record.
- **Allergies.**
  - The reaction type is decided from the reaction wording first (hives, rash, swelling and similar mean hypersensitivity), then from the source's `reaction_type`.
  - Mechanism is `immune` for allergy, `non_immune` for intolerance, and `unknown` otherwise.
- **Labs.**
  - Analytes are matched by LOINC, then by `nfm_code`, then by test name.
  - eGFR rows tagged African American are skipped. Both the 2009 non-AA and 2021 values are kept.
  - Non-numeric values (invalidated or hemolyzed) are dropped.
  - Units are converted, for example cells/uL to 10*3/uL. A result in a unit I can't convert is dropped.
